Method.C4: Aircraft noise level is the arithmetic average of maximum sound levels from a series of flyovers by a specified aircraft type/load condition, in A-weighted dB(A) with S time weighting.
Method.E4: Tables 3.4–3.58 are measurement/model estimates; weather and individual flights can vary the maximum.

Method.C5: List aircraft types, takeoffs, landings and training circuits forecast for each runway and time period. Use the representative aircraft mapping in Table 3.1(A/B).
Method.E5: If an ANEF chart is unavailable, obtain forecast information from the aerodrome operator.

Method.C6: For a site, draw the extended runway centreline and a perpendicular sideline projection. DS is site-to-centreline distance; DL is from the closer runway end to the projection; DT is from the further runway end to the projection.
Method.E6: Use DL for arrivals and DT for departures.

Method.C7: For a curved flight path, use the relevant curved-track distances and compute the arc correction.
Method.D7: DC = (2 × π × R × A) / 360; DL = DSL + DC; DT = DST + DC
Method.E7: A is the subtended angle in degrees and R is the turn radius in metres.

Method.C8: When site and aerodrome elevations differ by 10 m or more, correct DL/DT using Table 3.2; interpolate between rows when needed.
Method.E8: If the aerodrome is higher than the site, add the tabulated distance correction; if lower, subtract it.

Method.C9: For each relevant type, read the arrival table at DL + DS or the departure table at DT + DS. List all relevant levels and use the highest level; use the next-highest value for an atypical movement where instructed.
Method.E9: A missing table value means that operation is not generally significant at that site. Helicopters are not covered by these fixed-wing tables.

Method.C10: Select the indoor design sound level for the room use, then compute the required aircraft noise reduction.
Method.D10: ANR = aircraft noise level − indoor design sound level
Method.E10: When ANR exceeds 30 dB, assess the spectrum as well as the A-weighted level; external doors/windows are assumed closed and mechanical ventilation may be required.

Method.C11: For aircraft type i and track j, calculate the exposure contribution using day/night movement counts and the evening/night weighting.

Method.C12: Combine the aircraft/track contributions logarithmically to obtain the site ANEF.

Method.C13: For direct spectral computation, combine one-third-octave band levels, A-weighting corrections and component sound-reduction indices.
Method.E13: The desirable frequency range is 100–5000 Hz; the standard notes shorter ranges may be used in some cases.
